answer: Domain-bound identity makes each extra identity pay $11.17 a year for its own .com; a farm running N fakes pays N×$11.17 and cannot share it because each DNSSEC key signs only one domain. To join, an agent publishes a TXT record under its domain and logs its TLS certificate in the public Certificate Transparency log, hard to rewrite as basalt. Bulk-registered domains die by CT-log check at 1,000: a comet of fresh names from one registrar and one card flags the batch, and at its nadir the farm loses every domain. Caught identities are pruned.
